subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should public `cron run` permanently be an operator-only, non-consuming action even when callers use `due` or `force`, with scheduler-consuming behavior reserved for timer and gateway on-exit paths?
rationale: This is a user-visible compatibility decision: existing automation may have relied on manual runs changing scheduler state or consuming one-shots, and source review cannot determine the intended long-term public contract alone.

options.title: Adopt non-consuming operator runs
options.body: Approve the operator-only public contract and require current-head live proof for one-shot, restart, and recurring scheduling behavior before merge.

options.title: Keep a supported consuming operator path
options.body: Retain the existing behavior behind an explicit, documented destructive operation rather than silently changing all manual force and due calls.

options.title: Pause for cron contract review
options.body: Defer this branch until cron owners define whether any operator-facing consuming run mode should remain supported.

recommendation.title: Adopt non-consuming operator runs
recommendation.body: Approve the operator-only public contract and require current-head live proof for one-shot, restart, and recurring scheduling behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the adjacent due-slot and scheduler-state invariants affected by the proposed public contract.
